title: RAPID: Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations
why_read: A robotics paper that turns a single video demonstration into a verified, reusable robot program by having a coding agent write and refine trajectory-optimization code.
analysis: RAPID takes one human video demonstration and automatically infers a task specification, the low-level action primitives, and a way to test the resulting program, then uses an agentic code-generation loop to write and refine a robot program that reproduces the task. Rather than encoding raw motion, it represents the strategy in terms of object relationships and trajectory-optimization primitives, which the authors argue makes it generalize better across different object poses, shapes, and materials. It was tested on eight contact-rich manipulation tasks in simulation and successfully deployed on a real Franka robot arm. This is a genuinely useful direction for reducing the amount of hand-engineering needed to program robots for new manipulation tasks, though real-world robustness beyond the tested tasks remains to be seen.
